The impact depends on the XML processor layered above Expat and on how it splits expanded names; no downstream processor was analyzed. The advisory itself says exploits with code execution are known to exist.
Namespace processing must be enabled (XML_ParserCreateNS) for the vulnerable separator handling to apply.

The advisory says the concern is one or more separator characters in xmlns attribute values; the fix checks only whether the final byte of the URI equals the separator, which is the position that matters for the appended separator.
The OSV fixed event names the 2.4.5 release-preparation merge commit (97a48405), not the code fix a2fe525e; release tag ancestry and source were used to confirm the fix.
The MITRE CNA record is a placeholder (n/a vendor/product/version, no metrics or problemTypes); CVSS 9.8 and CWE-668 come from NVD.

critical_operation.description: addBinding scans the namespace URI only to compare it with the built-in XML and xmlns namespace names. It never looks for the namespace separator inside the URI. When namespace processing is enabled, len is then incremented to leave room for a separator and the URI is copied into the binding. An attacker-authored xmlns declaration can therefore place separator characters inside the URI; a processor above Expat that splits expanded names on that separator sees extra components and malformed or attacker-chosen tag names. The 2.4.5 fix rejects the URI with XML_ERROR_SYNTAX when it contains the separator.

entry_point.description: addBinding is called while parsing a namespace declaration (xmlns or xmlns:prefix) from the document prolog or an element. The URI value is attacker-controlled XML content; namespace processing must be enabled (XML_ParserCreateNS) for the separator to matter.
